_about: Fact fixes from the Reckon fact check of 20 Oct 2026 (project doc claude/reckon-factcheck-sample.md and the first-month check). Applied to Ballpark's bank, which Reckon shares. Each entry lists only the fields that change; tools/apply-ballpark-fixes.js checks every fact's current text first.

body:48.q: How many litres of fluid do the kidneys filter out of the blood in a day?

animals:94.q: How wide can an adult male orangutan’s arm span be, in metres?

science:30.q: What percentage of Dead Sea water, by weight, is dissolved salt?
science:30.n: About ten times as salty as the ocean, at 3.5%.

britain:31.q: About how many English words were first recorded in Shakespeare’s writing, according to the Oxford English Dictionary?
britain:31.n: Including “lonely”, “bedroom” and “eyeball”, though some may be older.

britain:94.q: At spring tides, how much does the tide rise and fall at London Bridge, in metres?

food:8.q: By Food Standards Agency figures, how much caffeine is in a mug of tea, in milligrams?
food:8.n: A weak brew can have about half that.

weather:84.q: At most, how much sunlight power reaches a square metre facing the Sun on a clear day at sea level, in watts?
weather:84.n: In Britain it is nearer 800 W at midsummer noon. Solar panels turn about a fifth of it into electricity.

body:58.n: 24 separate vertebrae plus the fused sacrum and coccyx. Babies start with 33.

britain:95.q: At its greatest, how much can the tide rise and fall in the Severn Estuary, in metres?
britain:95.n: The second-highest tidal range in the world, by most counts.

science:68.q: How hot is the main yellow part of a candle flame, in °C?
science:68.n: The faint blue zone near the wick is hotter, about 1,400 °C.

earth:86.q: How long is the Great Rift Valley, from Lebanon down to Mozambique, in kilometres?

science:31.n: Red is the longest-wavelength colour we can see.

weather:97.q: At its fastest, in 2012, how far did Greenland’s Jakobshavn glacier flow in a day, in metres?

food:64.q: Above about what temperature does the browning of toast and roast meat get going quickly, in °C?

animals:88.q: How far can monarch butterflies migrate, in kilometres?
animals:88.n: Up to about 4,800 km, from southern Canada to the forests of Mexico.

food:60.q: About how much does a single espresso hold, in millilitres?
food:60.n: Pushed through the coffee in about 25 seconds. The Italian standard is 25 ml.

everyday:94.q: How much does a full-size UK wheelie bin hold, in litres?
everyday:94.n: Many councils use smaller 180- or 140-litre bins.

science:69.q: How hot is the hottest part of a Bunsen burner’s blue flame, in °C?

animals:30.q: Up to how long can a sperm whale hold its breath, in minutes?

weather:96.q: On average, how thick is Arctic sea ice in winter, in metres?
weather:96.n: Ice that survives several summers can be 3 m or more.

science:39.q: In its 1975 form, every how many years did Moore’s law say the number of transistors on a chip would double?
science:39.n: Moore’s first version, in 1965, said every year. It held for about 50 years.

body:42.q: By the usual estimate, how long are all the blood vessels in an adult laid end to end, in kilometres?

everyday:56.q: How many small squares make up a chessboard?

food:70.n: An industry estimate: roughly 90 for every person.

weather:94.q: How cold is the top of a big thundercloud over Britain, in degrees below zero?
weather:94.n: The top spreads out into an anvil of ice crystals.

food:61.q: On average worldwide, how many litres of water, mostly rain, does it take to produce a kilogram of beef?
food:61.n: Most of it is rain that falls on the grass and crops the cattle eat.

everyday:96.q: What is the traditional term of a UK mortgage, in years?
everyday:96.n: Most first-time buyers now choose 30 years or more.

animals:93.n: The longest snake in the world; most adults are 3 to 5 m.

food:18.q: Roughly how many bananas does the UK eat in a year?
food:18.n: An often-quoted estimate; the most popular fruit in Britain.

body:10.q: About how many cells make up the body of an average adult man?
body:10.n: About 36 trillion by a 2023 count; a typical woman has about 28 trillion.

places:69.q: How many people lived in the City of Leeds council area at the 2021 census?

weather:66.q: What was the average sea surface temperature between 60°S and 60°N in 2024, in °C?
weather:66.n: A record for a calendar year, by Copernicus figures.

weather:15.q: What is the strongest wind gust ever recorded by a weather station, not counting tornadoes, in km per hour?

animals:16.q: About how much does a fully grown blue whale weigh, in tonnes?
animals:16.n: The heaviest ever weighed was nearer 190 tonnes.

animals:73.q: How long can an elephant live in the wild, in years?
animals:73.n: About as long as a person; the record in captivity is 86.

everyday:65.n: The original 74-minute disc was sized to fit Beethoven’s Ninth, as legend has it.
